transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because I feel like I’m falling apart, honestly. Ever since the foreclosure notices started showing up, I just… I haven’t been myself at all. I’ll be sitting in my truck before work crying, trying to pull it together before I go into the shop, and then the phone rings and I jump like something terrible is about to happen.

At work, I’m snapping at the apprentices over little things, and that’s not how I usually am. I work on heavy equipment, so you can’t be distracted or careless, and I’ve been making dumb mistakes in the repair bay—mistakes I never would’ve made before all this started. It’s like my nerves are shot and I can’t get my footing.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried most days, even when there isn’t a specific problem happening at that moment?

Yeah… I mean, it feels like it’s most days now. Ever since those foreclosure notices started coming, I feel like I’m just coming apart at the seams. Even if nothing is happening right that second, I’m still sitting there waiting for the next bad thing. Like I’ll be in my truck before work and I just start crying, trying to get myself together before I walk into the shop.

And then the phone rings and I jump like it’s going to be more terrible news. I know that probably sounds ridiculous, but my whole body reacts before I can even think. At work I’m on edge, too. I’ve been snapping at the apprentices over little stuff, and I hate that because that’s not really me. And I’m making stupid mistakes in the repair bay—things I never would’ve messed up before all this. It’s like I can’t shut the worry off, even when there isn’t an actual problem happening right in front of me.
Have you been feeling down or hopeless most days, or have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not just that I feel sad, it’s more like everything that used to keep me steady has just kind of fallen away. I used to be really involved outside of work — church volunteering, my fitness classes, even the truck-club outings. Those were things I showed up for without even thinking about it, like they were part of who I was. Lately I just… don’t go. I’ll tell myself I’m going to, and then I don’t get out the door.

And at work it’s gotten bad enough that they’ve taken me out of the high-risk repair bay, which was embarrassing. I’ve always been trusted with that kind of work, and now I’m not. That really hit me hard. So yeah, I guess I’ve lost interest, or maybe I just don’t have whatever it takes right now to keep doing the things I used to do.
Have you had any days where you felt down or hopeless nearly every day for most of the day, and this lasted for at least two weeks straight?

I’m not sure how to answer that cleanly. I’ve definitely had stretches where I felt really low and just… heavy, like I couldn’t see how things were going to get better. But “nearly every day for most of the day” and “two weeks straight” — I don’t know if I can say that exactly.

Some days it’s there from the minute I wake up, and it follows me around all day. Other days I’ll get distracted for a little while or I’ll be functional enough to get through what I have to do, and then it hits me again later. So I don’t want to overstate it and say yes if you mean literally most of the day every day for two full weeks. I haven’t really been tracking it that way. It’s been bad, but I’m not sure it fits that exact pattern.
Looking back, was there ever a time when you felt down or hopeless almost every day, all day, for at least two weeks in a row?

I honestly don’t know if I can say that, not the way you’re wording it. I mean, I can look back and say there were times I felt really down, like it was hanging over me most of the time, and I’d wake up already dreading the day. But “almost every day, all day, for two weeks in a row” feels hard for me to pin down.

I wasn’t exactly keeping track, you know? Some days felt completely awful, and then other days maybe I’d have a few hours where I was distracted or just pushing through, and I don’t know whether that counts or not. So I don’t want to say yes and make it sound more exact than I really remember. It’s been bad, but I’m not sure I can honestly say it was all day, nearly every day, for a full two weeks straight.
Have you noticed that you no longer get pleasure or satisfaction out of things you used to enjoy, like your volunteer work, fitness classes, or truck-club outings?

Yes… yeah, I have. Those exact things, actually. I used to get something out of them, not just because they were “activities,” but because they made me feel like myself. Church volunteering gave me a sense that I was useful, like I was showing up for people. Fitness classes made me feel strong and steady. And the truck-club outings were just… fun, you know? Being around people who understood that side of me, talking engines and builds and just having something to look forward to.

Now I mostly don’t go. I keep meaning to. I’ll think, “Okay, this week I’m going to get back to class,” or “I should show up at church, people are probably wondering where I am,” but then when it’s time, it just feels empty or like too much effort for something I’m not even sure I’ll enjoy. Same with the truck-club stuff — I used to be excited about it, and now I’ll see messages about an outing and just let it pass.

And it’s not only outside work. At work they’ve taken me out of the high-risk repair bay, and that’s been really hard because that was work I was trusted with. I took pride in that. So losing that, and then not showing up for the things I used to care about after work… it makes me feel like I’ve kind of dropped out of my own life.
Looking back, was there ever a period when you felt down or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row, even if you can’t say it was absolutely every single day?

I still don’t know that I can answer that with a clean yes. I understand you’re giving me a little more room there, like not absolutely every single day, but even then… I’m hesitant.

There have been periods where it felt like I was down most of the time, where the day had this gray cast over it and I was kind of dragging myself through. And if you asked me in the middle of one of those weeks, I probably would’ve said, “Yeah, I’m pretty much miserable.” But looking back and trying to say it was most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks in a row — I’m just not sure.

I can remember bad days grouped together. I can remember waking up already feeling defeated. But I can also remember times where I’d get pulled into something or have a stretch where I was functioning, or not thinking about it as much, and then later I’d crash back into feeling awful. So I don’t know how to count that.

I don’t want to dodge the question. It’s been really low at times. But I don’t feel confident saying, “Yes, definitely, that happened for at least two weeks straight.” I just don’t have that level of certainty about it.

Has there been a time when you completely stopped getting any enjoyment or satisfaction from things you used to really like, like your volunteer work, fitness classes, or truck-club outings — even for a week or more?

Yeah… I think that’s fair to say. Maybe “completely” is a strong word, because there might be little moments where I’m distracted or I can appreciate something in theory, but for a week or more at a time, yes — the things that used to actually give me satisfaction just haven’t felt worth showing up for.

I’ve stopped going to church volunteering, and that bothers me because I used to be pretty consistent with it. It wasn’t just something on the calendar — it made me feel useful, like I was part of something. Same with fitness classes. I used to keep up with them, and now I just don’t go. And the truck-club outings… I used to really look forward to those, and now I’ll see the messages or know there’s something happening, and I just let it pass.

And work is part of it too. I’ve been taken out of the high-risk repair bay, and that has hit me hard. That was the kind of work I took pride in, where I felt trusted and capable. So between that and not showing up for the things outside of work that used to matter to me, it really does feel like I’ve lost a lot of what made me feel like myself.

Has there been a time when you felt absolutely no interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like your volunteer work, fitness classes, or truck-club outings, for a period of two weeks or more?

I’m not sure I can say “absolutely no” for two weeks or more. That wording is hard for me, because I don’t know that I’ve been completely flat, like there was zero interest or zero pleasure every single day for that long.

What I can say is I’ve had stretches where those things felt so distant from me that I just didn’t go, or I didn’t want to go enough to make myself do it. Like I’d see something about the truck-club outing and instead of feeling that pull — the “oh, that’ll be fun” feeling — it was more like, “I can’t deal with that.” Or with fitness classes, I’d think about going and then it would feel pointless before I even got my shoes on. Same with volunteering — I’d know it mattered, but I didn’t feel connected to it the way I used to.

But if you’re asking specifically, “Was there a solid two-week period where there was absolutely no interest or pleasure at all,” I don’t know. I don’t feel comfortable saying yes to that. There may have been little moments where I felt something, or where I thought maybe I should care, even if I still didn’t follow through. So… I guess my honest answer is I’m not sure.

Can you think of any time when you felt no interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like your volunteer work, fitness classes, or truck-club outings, for a full two weeks without improvement?

I guess the clearest way I can answer is that I don’t know if I can measure it perfectly as “a full two weeks with no improvement,” but I can tell you the impact has been pretty obvious.

I’ve stopped showing up for things I used to be pretty steady with. Church volunteering, for one — I used to go and feel like I was useful there, like people counted on me, and now I just… don’t go. Fitness classes too. I used to keep those as part of my routine, and I’ve fallen off from them. And the truck-club outings, those were something I actually looked forward to, not just something to fill time, and now I let them pass even when I know they’re happening.

At work, it’s shown up too. I’ve been taken out of the high-risk repair bay, and that’s been really hard to swallow because that was the work where I felt competent and trusted. So whether or not I can say there was absolutely no pleasure for exactly two weeks, I can say I’ve pulled back from a lot of the things that used to matter to me, and it’s affected my work and my life outside of work pretty badly.
Have you had a period where you lost interest or pleasure in nearly all activities, not just the ones you mentioned, for most of the day, more days than not, for at least two weeks?

I’m not sure I can say that, no — not the way you’re wording it. “Nearly all activities,” “most of the day,” and “more days than not for at least two weeks” feels very specific, and I don’t know that I can honestly pin it down like that.

I know I’ve pulled away from the big things that used to matter to me, like the ones we talked about. And I know there have been days where I just don’t feel much pull toward anything, where even normal stuff feels kind of… flat or like too much effort. But I don’t know if that was nearly everything, most of the day, for a solid two weeks.

It’s more that my interest has been really inconsistent and a lot lower than it used to be. Some things I avoid, some things I think about doing but don’t follow through with, and maybe here and there I still get a small bit of interest or comfort from something. So I wouldn’t want to say yes if you mean a clear two-week stretch where almost nothing felt enjoyable most of the day. I just don’t know.

Has there been a time when you felt little or no interest in things you used to care about, like your volunteer work, fitness classes, or truck-club outings, and this lasted for several days in a row — not just one day or a few hours, but several days where nothing really felt worth doing?

Yeah… yes, I think I can say that. Maybe not in the perfect way you’re asking with exact days marked off on a calendar, but there have definitely been several days in a row where I just couldn’t get myself to care enough to do the things I normally would’ve cared about.

It’s not just that I missed one fitness class because I was tired, or skipped one truck-club outing because something came up. It’s more like I’d see the reminder or know it was happening, and instead of feeling interested, I’d just think, “What’s the point?” or “I can’t deal with being around people.” And then I wouldn’t go. Same with church volunteering — I used to keep up with that, and it mattered to me, but I’ve stopped showing up there too.

And at work, it’s been hard because I’ve been taken out of the high-risk repair bay. That was a big part of how I saw myself there, like I was trusted to handle the serious stuff, and now not being in that role makes everything feel even more… I don’t know, like I’m not really myself. So yes, there have been stretches of several days where things that used to feel worth doing just didn’t feel worth the effort.

Looking back, was there ever a continuous period of at least two weeks where you felt a clear loss of interest or pleasure in most things you used to enjoy, even if it wasn’t every single day of that time?

I still don’t know that I can say that clearly, even looking back. I mean, I can tell you there were stretches where I was really withdrawn and things I normally cared about didn’t seem worth the effort, but when you say “a continuous period of at least two weeks” and “most things,” I get stuck.

Part of me wants to say maybe, because it has felt like this has gone on and on, and I’ve definitely pulled away from a lot. But if I’m being accurate, I don’t have a neat two-week block in my head where I can say, yes, during that whole time I had a clear loss of interest or pleasure in most things. It’s more uneven than that. Some days are really flat, some days I can still get a little interested in something or feel okay for a bit, and then it drops off again.

So I guess my answer is: I’m not sure. I’ve had several-day stretches where things didn’t feel worth doing, but I can’t honestly say I remember a continuous two weeks like that.

Looking back, has there been a period of at least two weeks where you generally lost interest or pleasure in most of the things you used to enjoy, even if there were some small moments of interest or pleasure during that time?

I’m still hesitant to say yes to that in a clean way. I know you’re making room for “small moments,” which helps, but even then… I don’t have a clear two-week stretch in my mind where I can confidently say I generally lost interest or pleasure in most things.

It’s more like I’ve had runs of days where I’m really checked out, where the things I normally care about just don’t pull me at all. And then there might be a little window where something feels okay, or I think maybe I’ll do something, and then I don’t follow through, or the feeling fades. So when I look back, it feels messy and uneven, not like a solid block of time I can point to.

I don’t want to overstate it just because things have been bad. I can say my interest has dropped a lot, and I’ve been avoiding a lot of things I used to enjoy. But a definite “at least two weeks, most things, generally lost interest or pleasure” — I’m not sure I can honestly say that.
Looking back, has there been a time when you felt down or low most of the day, more often than not, for at least two weeks — even if there were some better moments during that time?

I’m not sure how to answer that cleanly. I mean, I’ve definitely felt low, and there have been days where it feels like it sits on me for a lot of the day, not just a little passing mood. But when you say “most of the day, more often than not, for at least two weeks,” I start trying to line it up in my head and I don’t know that I can honestly pin it down like that.

It hasn’t felt simple or steady, if that makes sense. There are days where I wake up already feeling kind of sunk, and it follows me through work or through the evening, and then there might be a better patch where I’m distracted or I feel more like myself for a bit. Then later it can come back. So looking back, it all blends together, but I can’t confidently say, yes, there was a definite two-week period where I was down most of the day on most days.

I don’t want to make it sound lighter than it is, because it has been rough. But I also don’t want to say something too definite just because I’m upset sitting here talking about it. So I guess my honest answer is: maybe, but I’m not sure. I know I’ve had a lot of low days. I just can’t clearly say it met that exact two-week pattern.
Looking back, has there been a time when you lost interest or felt no pleasure in nearly everything you used to enjoy, even for a week or more?

I don’t think I can say “nearly everything,” even for a week, not in a way that feels accurate. I know I’ve had times where I just didn’t want to do much, and things that usually help me feel a little better didn’t really grab me. Like, I might think about doing something I normally enjoy and then just feel like it’s too much effort, or like I wouldn’t get anything out of it anyway.

But “lost interest or felt no pleasure in nearly everything” sounds so complete, and I’m not sure that’s what it’s been. There have still been little moments where something gets through, or I can be distracted for a bit, or I don’t feel totally shut off. It’s not like everything went blank across the board for a solid week that I can clearly point to.

So… I’d say I’ve had days, maybe several days in a row, where I felt really disconnected from things I usually enjoy. But I don’t know that I can honestly say it was nearly everything for a week or more.
Looking back, has there been a time when you felt down or low for at least two weeks straight, even if there were some small improvements during that time?

I’m having a hard time saying yes to “two weeks straight.” I know I’ve already been kind of circling around that, but that’s honestly where I am with it.

There have definitely been stretches where I felt low over and over, like it kept coming back and I couldn’t really shake it, and some days it felt like it was there from the time I got up until pretty late in the day. But when you say “at least two weeks straight,” even with little improvements, I start trying to measure it and I don’t trust my memory enough to say it was continuous like that.

It’s more that things have felt heavy in waves. A few bad days, then maybe a day or part of a day where I could function a little more normally or not think about it as much, and then it would slide back again. So I don’t want to make it sound like I was fine, because I wasn’t. But I also don’t want to say there was a definite two-week straight period if I can’t really point to it.

So I guess my answer is… I’m not sure. Maybe there were times close to that, but I can’t honestly say I know there was a solid two weeks straight of feeling down or low.
Looking back, has there been a time when you felt down or low most days for at least two weeks, even if there were a few hours here or there when you felt slightly better?

I know you’re asking it a little differently, and I’m trying to be careful with the wording because I don’t want to overstate it. “Most days for at least two weeks” is maybe easier to think about than “two weeks straight,” but I still don’t feel totally confident saying yes.

There have been periods where, looking back, it felt like more days than not I was low. Like it wasn’t just one bad afternoon and then gone. It would show up again and again, and even when I could get through things or have a few hours where I wasn’t focused on it as much, it didn’t feel like I was really back to normal. But whether that clearly lasted two full weeks, with most days being that way… I don’t know. I keep trying to count it in my head and it gets blurry.

So I guess the most honest answer is that it may have happened, or it may have been close to that, but I can’t point to a definite two-week stretch and say, yes, that was most days. I can say I’ve had a lot of low days, and some stretches felt pretty relentless, but I’m not sure it meets that exact time frame.

Looking back, has there ever been a time when you lost interest or felt no pleasure in nearly all of your usual activities — even for a period of two weeks, even if there were small moments of interest or pleasure during that time?

I get what you’re asking, and I know it’s close to what you asked before, but the “two weeks” part and “nearly all” part still trips me up.

I’ve definitely had periods where things I usually like just didn’t feel worth doing. Like I’d think, okay, maybe I should watch something, or go do something small, or call someone, or tinker with something, and then it would just feel flat before I even started. Not exactly like I hated everything, more like the spark wasn’t there and I couldn’t make myself care the way I normally would.

But if I’m being honest, I don’t know that I can say it was nearly all of my usual activities for a whole two-week period. There were still small moments where something distracted me or I got a little interest back, even if it didn’t last long. And my memory of it isn’t clean enough for me to say, yes, for two weeks most everything gave me no pleasure.

So… I’d say I’ve had stretches where I felt pretty shut down and uninterested, but I can’t confidently say it was nearly all activities for two weeks.

Looking back, has there ever been a two-week period where you generally lost interest or felt no pleasure in most of the things you used to enjoy, even if there were a few small moments when you felt a little better during that time?

I know we’ve kind of been circling the same thing, and I’m sorry if I’m not giving you a clean answer. I’m really trying to answer it the way you mean it, not just say yes because parts of it feel familiar.

When you put it as “generally lost interest” in “most things,” I can say there have been times where that feels pretty close. Like, things I normally use to unwind or look forward to just didn’t pull me in. I’d have the thought that I should do something I usually like, and then it would feel like too much effort or like there was no point. Not dramatic exactly, just kind of flat and empty.

But the two-week part is still where I hesitate. I don’t have a clear block of time in my head where I can say, yes, for two weeks that was true most of the time. It may have happened. It might have been close. But I honestly don’t know. There were little moments where I could get interested in something briefly or feel a little lighter, and then later I’d feel shut down again, so it’s hard for me to sort out whether that counts as a full two-week period or not.

So I guess my answer is: I’ve definitely had stretches of feeling disconnected from things I normally enjoy, but I can’t confidently say there was a definite two-week period where I lost pleasure in most things.
